meta.description: Prefabricated office cabins in six sizes, 10×10 ft to 40×10 ft, ex-GST prices published. Bolted panel modules that dismantle, move and join into bays.

hero.size_selector_label: Choose your size - six bolted panel modules
hero.short_description: A prefabricated office cabin is an office built as numbered steel panels, bolted together on a module grid rather than welded shut in one piece. Panels arrive on a transport break seam, bolt up at spline joints, and can be unbolted again when the site closes, so the same cabin moves to the next project or joins a neighbour through a site joining strip to form a multi-bay office. It is bought by project buyers, layout planners and installation crews who expect the office to be dismantled, extended or relocated inside its working life. Six approved sizes run from 10×10 ft at 100 sq ft to 40×10 ft at 400 sq ft, each with its own general arrangement drawing, opening schedule and staged desk count, priced ex-GST for the office module framework.

section2.h2: Why a Bolted Panel Office Cabin Costs More Than a Welded One
section2.paragraph1: Every cabin here is priced from a base rate of ₹1,300 per sq ft at 200 sq ft, against ₹1,250 on the Readymade Office Cabin range for the same six sizes at the same 8.5 ft height. The difference is the joint, not the finish. A readymade cabin is welded into one unit and craned into place whole. A prefabricated office cabin is drawn as a panel module grid: panels numbered, every junction a bolted spline joint, with a transport break seam that lets the shell come apart in planned pieces.
section2.paragraph2: That buys a second life. The cabin unbolts when the project closes, stacks flat, and re-erects on a new datum; it widens by adding a bay through the site joining strip instead of buying a second unit; a damaged cassette is a panel swap, not cutting work. Against that, the quoted price covers the module framework only: craneage, site joining, sanitary fit-out and multi-unit integration are quoted separately.
section2.cta: Send your size and site for a fixed quote

split_card.h3: One module today, a multi-bay office next year
split_card.paragraph1: The 20×10 ft cabin is drawn around a module grid datum, not a fixed outline. Its corner interface plates and site joining strip repeat on all six sizes, so a second module lands on that datum without re-cutting a shell.
split_card.paragraph2: That is why every opening is fixed per size and published below. A bay you may join later must know today which wall carries the door and where the partition lands. The GA drawing settles both before production release.

section3.h2: Compare the Six Prefabricated Office Cabin Sizes and Prices
section3.intro: Six approved sizes, one bolted panel platform, one price rule. Each shows its GA drawing, its opening schedule and its staged desks.

sizes.h3: 10×10 ft Prefabricated Office Cabin: 100 sq ft, Four Desks
sizes.paragraph: The smallest module on the panel platform and the only one whose entrance wall carries no glazing at all. Wall A is a door and nothing else, which leaves three solid panel runs a fit-out can use for a board, a switchboard or shelving without working around a window head. Buy it as the repeatable unit: a gate office, a stores office or a supervisor's room that will be unbolted and moved when the phase ends. Four desks are staged in the drawing; the price is for the module framework.

sections.h2: Prefabricated office cabin or prefab office building?

items.text: Two quite different things are searched for with the words prefabricated office. The first is a prefabricated office building: a steel-frame structure erected on a foundation, sized in thousands of square feet, competing with conventional construction. The second is a prefabricated office cabin: a finished steel room of 100 to 400 square feet that arrives on a trailer, is set on supports and is working the same day. This page is the second thing only, and every figure below describes a cabin.

If a foundation, a design team and a building permit are already part of the plan, the Prefab Buildings and Pre-Engineered Buildings ranges are where that requirement belongs. If the office has to exist on ground that will be handed back, or has to follow a project from one alignment to the next, a cabin is the right instrument and the whole page applies.

The word prefabricated does a second job here that portable does not. Every steel cabin SAMAN builds is portable, because it lifts and travels. Only some are prefabricated in the strict sense of being assembled on site from separately manufactured panels. That distinction is the reason this page exists as its own product rather than as a synonym of the Portable Office Cabin hub, and it is what the next section describes.

sections.h2: What makes a cabin prefabricated rather than portable

items.text: A readymade office cabin leaves the works as one welded box. The frame is welded, the sheets are fixed to the frame, the interior is finished inside the finished shell, and the unit is craned onto a trailer complete. It is a good product and it is the cheaper of the two, because welding a shell once is less work than detailing a shell that must come apart.

A prefabricated office cabin is drawn the other way round. The shell is set out on a module grid datum, and the walls, roof and floor are made as separately numbered panels that meet at bolted spline joints. A transport break seam is drawn where the shell is intended to divide. Corner interface plates locate the panels against each other, and a site joining strip closes the junction between one module and the next.

The consequences are practical rather than theoretical. A panel that is bolted can be unbolted, so the cabin can be taken down, stacked flat and re-erected rather than being craned whole down a road that may not take it. A junction that is drawn can be repeated, so a second module can be brought against the first later without cutting either shell. A numbered panel can be replaced, so a wall damaged by a reversing truck is a panel swap and not a fabrication job on a live site.

None of that removes the crane from the first delivery. These cabins are still lifted by four corner eye plates, one at each top corner, and still travel on an open trailer. What changes is what happens after the first placement, which is the part of the cost a project buyer usually meets twice.

sections.h2: Prefabricated, readymade or small: which page you need

items.text: SAMAN publishes three office cabin pages that a buyer can reasonably confuse, and the six sizes on this page appear on two of them. The difference is not the size ladder; it is the construction and the price rule.

The Readymade Office Cabin range carries the same six sizes as welded units at a base rate of ₹1,250 per sq ft at 200 sq ft. Buy from that page when the office is going to one place and staying there, when the budget matters more than the second move, and when nobody expects to add a bay.

This page carries the same six sizes as bolted panel modules at ₹1,300 per sq ft at 200 sq ft, roughly four per cent more. Buy from this page when the office is expected to be dismantled, relocated or extended, when the site has an access route that argues for delivering a shell in pieces, or when a multi-bay run is already on the drawing board.

The Small Office Cabin page is a different question again. It starts at 8×6 ft and 48 square feet and covers the one-person and two-person rooms this page does not publish at all. If the whole requirement is a gate clerk or a single supervisor, that page is cheaper and better fitted. This page starts at 100 square feet because a panel module below that size costs more to detail than it saves.

Container Offices sit outside all three. A container office is built from or like an ISO shipping container, with corner castings and a container frame. Nothing on this page is a container: the base is a plain steel skid and the corner fitting is a compact one-hole lifting eye plate. If a container shell is what is wanted, the Container Offices range is the right cluster.

sections.h2: How to choose between 100 and 400 square feet

items.text: Start from the number of people who sit inside on an ordinary working day, then check what the plot allows, then read the opening schedule to confirm the walls suit the fit-out.

One to four people at fixed desks fit the 10×10 ft at 100 square feet. Three people on ground that is long and narrow fit the 20×8 ft, which is the only 8 ft body on the page and the only one-way roof. A team of five with a manager who needs a door takes the 20×10 ft, and the 20×12 ft is the same plan for the same team where the circulation in a 10 ft body is too tight. Twelve people in one undivided room take the 30×10 ft. Eight people plus two managers who each need their own room take the 40×10 ft.

The opening schedule matters more than it looks. The 10×10 ft is the only size whose entrance wall carries no window at all, which makes it the easiest size to line with boards, racking or a switchboard. Every other size puts a window either side of the door on the entrance wall, which is better for daylight and worse for wall-mounted equipment. The two largest sizes carry two external doors rather than one, which is what allows a twelve-desk room and a package office to be evacuated sensibly.

The table below is every published size with the facts that decide between them. Prices are ex-GST for the module framework; the GST-inclusive figure for each size is shown on the size selector above.

sections.h2: What the bolted joint changes on your site

items.text: Four details on the general arrangement drawings are what a site actually handles, and each of them is drawn before production rather than resolved on site.

The module grid datum is the line everything else is measured from. It is why a second module can be set against the first years later and still meet it squarely, and it is why the opening positions on this page are published as coordinates from End C rather than as a description.

The bolted spline joint is the junction between two panels. It is designed to be opened, which is a different requirement from a joint that only has to be closed once, and it is the reason the panel schedule and the panel numbering exist as a document handed over with the cabin.

The transport break seam is where the shell is intended to divide for a road move. Knowing where it is before the first delivery is what turns a second move from an improvisation into a planned operation.

The site joining strip closes the gap when two modules stand side by side. It is the same detail on all six sizes, which is the whole reason a 20×10 ft office bought this year can grow into a two-bay office next year rather than being replaced.

items: Module grid datum: every opening on this page is dimensioned from End C, so a later bay meets the first squarely
Bolted spline joint: panel junctions are designed to be opened, not only closed once
Transport break seam: the shell divides where the drawing says, so a second move is planned rather than improvised
Site joining strip: the same junction detail on all six sizes, which is what lets one module become two bays
Corner interface plates and panel numbering: a damaged wall is a panel swap, not fabrication on a live site

sections.h2: Roof, lifting and transport across the six sizes

items.text: Five of the six sizes carry a centred ridge running the full length of the cabin, with two planes falling across the width and a ridge rise of only five to six inches above each eave. The roof reads almost level and is drawn that way deliberately: a shallow fall keeps the transport height down and keeps the panel run above the eaves uninterrupted, which matters on a shell that is meant to come apart.

The 20×8 ft is the exception. Its roof is a single one-way plane falling across the 8 ft width with the same five to six inches of total fall, no ridge, and straight eaves on both long walls. On a body only eight feet wide a ridge would buy nothing and would complicate the panel run.

Lifting is identical across all six. Four compact one-hole eye plates sit at the four top corners, H1 to H4, and nowhere else. There is no mid-span hook and no ridge hook, and there are no ISO corner castings, because these are not container-derived units. Every size is 8.5 ft nominal in height, which is what keeps the loaded trailer inside normal road clearances.

sections.h2: What the price covers and what is quoted separately

items.text: The published price is the office module framework in the approved size, with its drawn openings, its internal finish and its electrical provision as scheduled on the general arrangement drawing. It is quoted ex-GST; 18 per cent GST is added at invoice and both figures are shown on the size selector.

The price rule is arithmetic, not negotiation. A base rate of ₹1,300 per square foot applies at 200 square feet. Below that, smaller areas carry a band uplift because the fixed content of a cabin does not shrink with its floor: 100 to 149 square feet adds 15 per cent, 150 to 199 adds 10 per cent. Above 200, larger areas take a band reduction: 201 to 300 takes 4 per cent off, 301 to 400 takes 5 per cent off. That is where each of the six rates on this page comes from and it can be checked against the area in the table above.

What is not in the price is stated rather than implied. Craneage and offloading at your site, joining two or more modules together, any sanitary or plumbing fit-out, special performance evidence such as certified test data for a particular exposure, and multi-unit integration works are quotation items. Site preparation, the supporting pad and the incoming electrical supply are the buyer's scope.

Warranty period and exclusions are confirmed in the final quotation for your order. The general arrangement drawings on this page are buyer-facing control drawings and are marked not for fabrication: approved shop drawings, project engineering, the final load schedule and the signed quotation govern what is built.

sections.h2: Frequently asked questions about prefab office cabins

items.q: What is a prefabricated office cabin?
items.a: A steel office room made as numbered panels that bolt together on a module grid, rather than being welded into one box. It arrives on a trailer, is lifted by four corner eye plates and can be unbolted and re-erected on another site.

items.q: What is the price of a prefabricated office cabin in India?
items.a: SAMAN publishes six sizes ex-GST: 10×10 ft at ₹1,49,500, 20×8 ft at ₹2,28,800, 20×10 ft at ₹2,60,000, 20×12 ft at ₹2,99,520, 30×10 ft at ₹3,74,400 and 40×10 ft at ₹4,94,000. GST at 18% is added at invoice.

items.q: What sizes do prefabricated office cabins come in?
items.a: Six approved sizes from 100 to 400 square feet: 10×10, 20×8, 20×10, 20×12, 30×10 and 40×10 ft, all 8.5 ft nominal in height. Each has its own general arrangement drawing, opening schedule and staged desk count.

items.q: What is the difference between prefabricated and readymade office cabins?
items.a: A readymade cabin is welded into one finished unit and costs less. A prefabricated cabin is bolted from numbered panels, so it can be dismantled, moved and joined to a second module later. The bolted version is priced about four per cent higher.

items.q: Can a prefabricated office cabin be dismantled and moved?
items.a: Yes. The panels meet at bolted spline joints and the shell divides at a drawn transport break seam, so the cabin can be taken down, stacked flat and re-erected on a new datum. Craneage and site joining for the move are quoted separately.

items.q: Can two prefabricated office cabins be joined together?
items.a: Yes. All six sizes carry the same corner interface plates and site joining strip, so a second module can be brought against the first and closed at the junction. Multi-unit integration is a quotation item, not part of the published price.

items.q: Is a prefabricated office cabin the same as a container office?
items.a: No. A container office is built from or like an ISO shipping container with corner castings. These cabins sit on a plain steel skid and use compact one-hole lifting eye plates. Container-derived offices are on the Container Offices pages.

items.q: What is not included in the published cabin price?
items.a: Craneage and offloading, joining modules together, sanitary or plumbing fit-out, special performance evidence and multi-unit integration are quotation items. Site preparation, the supporting pad and the incoming electrical supply are the buyer's scope.

narrative: These specifications describe a panelised office module, so they are read in a different order from a welded cabin's. Group B is the one that decides the product: it records the joint, the panel schedule and the lifting arrangement that make the shell demountable. Group C then fixes what those panels contain, size by size, because a panel run cannot be numbered until the openings in it are settled.

Group A is the commercial ladder and the arithmetic behind it. The rate for any size is the ₹1,300 per sq ft base at 200 sq ft with one band adjustment applied for area, so a rate can be checked rather than taken on trust. Group D is the platform material key shared with every SAMAN cabin family; nothing in it is specific to this page and nothing in it changes because the shell bolts rather than welds.

Group E is the scope boundary, and on a demountable product it is the group most worth reading before ordering. Joining modules, craning them, and integrating more than one unit are the operations this construction makes possible, and they are quoted separately from the module framework in every case.
